title: Germany's Ostpolitik Got a Rebrand, But Not a Comeback
gist: Podcast episode notes: Ian Klinke and Jakub Eberle argue Ostpolitik has migrated to the far-right AfD as identity politics rather than policy, and that AfD state-election gains are unlikely to reverse Germany's post-2022 hardline Russia policy. They pose the question of what Germany should do if pivoting to neither Russia nor the US.

insights.claim: Germany's historical Ostpolitik strategy of engagement with Russia now lives on in the far-right Alternative für Deutschland, functioning as identity politics rather than as actual policy.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Rhetorical Russia-friendliness from AfD may not translate into policy shifts that matter for sanctions or energy.
insights.quote: has found a new home in the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), not as policy, but as identity politics

insights.claim: Despite strong AfD results in recent state elections, the guests doubt these wins will reverse Germany's stricter Russia policy that solidified after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Suggests continuity of German Russia policy (sanctions, energy decoupling) despite far-right electoral momentum.
insights.quote: aren't confident that victory will suddenly reverse Germany's stricter Russia policy

insights.claim: The guests frame Germany's interests as lying in pivoting toward neither Russia nor the United States, implying a search for a third strategic path.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Hints at German/European strategic autonomy debates that shape defense spending and transatlantic alignment.
